minutes.headline: Sewer Commission previewed its rate-increase pitch for town meeting; says the override won't affect its budget
minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission reviewed a rate-increase slideshow prepared for the town meeting/override vote, covering cost drivers, declining betterments, and reliance on user charges, while stressing an effort to keep minimum charges low for seniors and lower-income residents. Members also got updates on the manhole repair, a completed tie-in bid at 5 Ramgren Road, an unresolved sewer stub search at 100 Laurel Lane, and confirmed the sewer department is self-funded and would not be affected by the town override's outcome.

what_happened.line: The Commission previewed the sewer rate-increase slideshow it will present at town meeting, citing disposal costs and shrinking betterment revenue as drivers.
Staff said the sewer department is self-funded through user charges and would not be cut regardless of whether the town override passes.
The lowest of three or four bids was selected for the 5 Ramgren Road sewer tie-in, and work is expected to start soon.
Staff said they still cannot locate the sewer stub for 100 Laurel Lane and plan to dig to confirm whether the town owes the property a new one.
Staff confirmed the late-payment interest rate has not been raised and said the effort was to keep the minimum sewer charge low for seniors and lower-income residents.

why_it_matters: Sewer ratepayers face a rate increase that will be presented at town meeting; the size of that increase is on the slideshow the minutes describe but is not restated here.
Because the sewer fund is self-supporting through user fees, the outcome of the separate town override vote will not change sewer rates or service.
A property owner at 100 Laurel Lane may be owed a new sewer stub at town expense if the existing one cannot be located, which the commission is still investigating.
watch_next: Next meeting, May 12, 2026: quarter four billing commitment and town meeting feedback are scheduled agenda items.
Resolution of the 100 Laurel Lane sewer stub search remains open and undecided.
